text:
About three-fifths of the world’s people (roughly 60%) lived in countries with per capita income of $1230 or less in 1997. China and India alone were about 37% of world population and both sat well under that line (China roughly $750–860, India roughly $400), and Indonesia, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nigeria, and most of sub-Saharan Africa add another billion-plus people who were also under it. That is on the order of 3.5 billion of about 5.85 billion, so neither 40% nor 25% fits.
CONFIDENCE: 74
